Q: Cronjob every 25 hours? A:

It's possible depends on your needs. I'm using heavy Google API service task which quickly encrease my 10k units daily quota which updates every day (24 hours from last exceed), so what I'm done with it is measured how long will it take for the limit to be exceeded, in my situation it takes about an hour, so if I run my cron task for example in 17:00 and it exceeded quta limit in 18:00 (conditionally) - I need to create a new cron task at 18:00 (* 18 * * *) (or every time after 18 o'clock, it's up to you) every day which means that after every this task launch quota limit will already be updated to continue the fun. Thus this does not depend on the specific hours number the job is started.

Q: Understanding older Spring Boot REST API style using @Controller + @ResponseBody A:

This particular project actually started around 4–5 years ago, so I was surprised to still see patterns like `@Controller + @ResponseBody` and manual `JSONObject` handling instead of more modern DTO-based REST style.

* focus on controller/service/repository flow?

Q: Digtal Garden / Portfolio-Showcase Site, which arch and tools to choose? A:

I am voting for Astro here.

  • Keeping them in one place makes bundling, version locking, and global backups significantly easier.
  • Framework: You can truly build a functional website just by reading their official documentation over a weekend.
  • If you are looking for solid color palettes and clean typography baselines, you can check out Google's AI webpages.
  • Content depth trumps beautiful pixels every single time. If your thoughts are structured, your public repositories are rich, and your documentation is useful, people won’t care about flashy animations. In fact, an extremely simple and lightning-fast text interface often makes you look like an efficient, non-conformist engineer who prioritizes substance over form.
